prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1038; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you understand this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Great. Can you describe what happened at the intersection in Houston?

A: I was driving through the intersection on a green light. I had just passed the crosswalk when a vehicle coming from my right ran the red light and hit the driver's side of my car.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I glanced over when I heard the horn, but it was already too late to stop.

Q: How fast would you estimate you were traveling?

A: Maybe 30 or 35 miles per hour. The light had just turned green, so I wasn't going very fast.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No, I stayed conscious. My head didn't hit anything, but my body was thrown against the seatbelt and then sideways into the door.

Q: Did you get medical attention after the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic later that afternoon. They diagnosed me with neck and back strain.

Q: Where are you experiencing pain now?

A: My neck is stiff and sore, especially when I turn my head to the left. My lower back aches when I sit for long periods, and I've had some tightness in my shoulders.

Q: Are you currently receiving any treatment?

A: I've been going to physical therapy twice a week, and the clinic gave me muscle relaxers and anti-inflammatories.

Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before this accident?

A: I had some occasional back stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing that stopped me from working or doing my normal activities.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'm still hoping to get back to full strength.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
